Giambatista Beccaria, Erasmus Darwin, Adam Walker, and Luke Howard. The role assigned
to electricity in the life-cycle of clouds, for example, appears to inform the second stanza; and
S. shows a clear understanding of the process of atmospheric evaporation — condensation
— precipitation. What is specifically owing to modern science in the images of The Cloud is
not always easy to identify, however. That clouds were the product of evaporation and con-
densation, for example, had been speculated upon since antiquity. In De Re. Nat. Lucretius
notes that ‘The clouds also often take up a great deal of seawater besides . . . when the winds
carry clouds above the great sea’ (vi 503–5); while Pliny held that ‘clouds are formed out of
moisture rising to a height or air condensed into moisture’ (Hist. Nat. II xlii 111).
